name: Treaty with the Apache, 1852 (Treaty of Santa Fe)
aka: Treaty with the Apache Nation, July 1, 1852
area: Apache country in New Mexico Territory (present New Mexico and Arizona); the treaty ceded no land, so Royce has no cession for it.
presentDayTribes: Fort Sill Apache Tribe of Oklahoma
Mescalero Apache Tribe of the Mescalero Reservation, New Mexico
nations: Chiricahua Apache (Mangas Coloradas, a Chiricahua chief per the Indian Claims Commission, signed; his signing was witnessed separately by Bvt. Capt. John Pope)
Apache bands led by the other signing chiefs, Capitan Vuelta, Cuentas Azules, Blancito, Negrito and Capitan Simon
promises: Article 9: the United States would, at its earliest convenience, designate, settle and adjust the Apaches' territorial boundaries.
Article 10: the United States would give donations, presents and implements and adopt other liberal and humane measures as it judged proper.
Article 2: perpetual peace between the Apache and the United States.
Article 4: the Apache would refer all aggressions against themselves or their property and territory to the United States for adjustment.

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission found that, despite the undertaking in this treaty to designate, settle and adjust the Apaches' territorial boundaries, the United States never carried out that obligation. It found that no treaty of cession with the Chiricahua ever became operative and that their lands were taken without consent or compensation, the taking completed on September 4, 1886.

breaches.quote: this obligation was never carried out by the United States

breaches.what: Final judgment of $15,967,300.00 to the Fort Sill Apache Tribe and the Chiricahua plaintiffs on their claims in Dockets 30-A and 48-A, entered on a stipulation of the parties adopted by the Commission. A stipulated judgment is not a finding of breach; the finding is the 1968 one above.

compensation: No land payment under this treaty. The Chiricahua claims for their aboriginal lands ended in a $15,967,300.00 judgment entered on a stipulation in 1971 (Dockets 30-A and 48-A).
today: The Chiricahua removal and the revocation of their reservation are recorded under cession-1876-10-30-apache. The Fort Sill Apache Tribe says it has since acquired small pieces of land in its home territory in New Mexico and Arizona.

nationVoice.summary: Tells its history as that of Chiricahua survivors imprisoned in Florida and Alabama and then at Fort Sill, about a third of whom kept demanding the lands they had been promised.

openQuestions: Which present-day nations descend from the five eastern signers was not settled; the Mescalero and Jicarilla are listed as likely, not confirmed.
The 1855 Meriwether treaties with the Mescalero and Gila Apache, never ratified, are in the OSU database and may deserve extra- files.

Audit 2026-11-08: the 1971 final judgment was changed from 'claims-commission' to 'litigation' because it was entered on a stipulation; the 1968 finding (Finding 10(e) and Finding 11) still carries the broken status. The statement that Mangas Coloradas signed at Acoma on July 11, 1852, and the description of the other signers as bands east of the Rio Grande, were removed: neither the treaty text nor the ICC findings opened say so.
